Validate inference embedding model before checking for existing uses

This commit changes the order of two steps when creating an inference
endpoint in TransportPutInferenceModelAction. The validation call is now
performed prior to checking for existing index mappings using the
inference endpoint ID, since if dimensions are not specified by the user
when creating a text_embedding or embedding endpoint, then attempting to
create a MinimalServiceSettings from the request will throw, because
dimensions are required in the MinimalServiceSettings constructor.

The validation call will populate the dimensions for the model via a
call to updateModelWithEmbeddingDetails(), meaning that the dimensions
are guaranteed to be non-null when TransportPutInferenceModelAction
checks for existing uses of the inference endpoint ID.

commit_message:
Forbid index-scoped deprecated settings

Support for index-scoped settings depends on the index-created version,
not the current cluster version, so it isn't appropriate to use
`Property.Deprecated` for these settings. Instead we must use one of the
versioned values such as`IndexSettingDeprecatedInV9AndRemovedInV10`.

This commit adds a validation rule to forbid this inappropriate
combination of properties on settings.

commit_message:
fix: use safe stringification for status code error messages

Replace JSON.stringify(code) with a safe stringifyStatusCode() helper
in res.status() to prevent TypeError when non-serializable values
like BigInt or Symbol are passed as status codes.

JSON.stringify(BigInt(200)) throws 'TypeError: Do not know how to
serialize a BigInt', which overrides the intended 'Invalid status code'
error message. The new helper handles BigInt, Symbol, null-prototype
objects, and all other types safely.

Fixes: #6756

fix: handle unknown Content-Type in res.set() falling back to original value

When mime.contentType() returns false for unrecognized types,
res.set('Content-Type', value) was setting the header to the
literal string 'false'. This change falls back to the original
value, matching how res.type() already handles this case.

Fixes: #7034

commit_message:
fix(redirect): throw TypeError instead of deprecating on missing/invalid url

Fixes #6941

Instead of sending a malformed Location header with 'undefined' or deprecated values, res.redirect() now throws a TypeError immediately when called without a valid url argument or with invalid argument types.

This is a breaking change for v6.x as indicated by the 'deprecate' label on the issue.

BREAKING CHANGE: res.redirect() now throws TypeError instead of deprecating:
- res.redirect() with no arguments
- res.redirect(undefined)
- res.redirect(url) where url is not a string
- res.redirect(status) where status is not a number

[Flight] Fix stranded row content under Node stream backpressure (#36516)

The Flight Server emits Text and TypedArray rows as two chunks: a header
that gives the row's id, type, and content length, followed by the
content itself. These two chunks were pushed into

items, so when the destination signaled backpressure between them, the

flushed those queues first — splicing the newly-arrived bytes into the

content. From there the Flight Client read rows from the wrong byte
offsets and the model failed to deserialize.

  Conv3d↔Linear, Ernie pair, _IdentityOp, Fp8Quantize/Fp8Dequantize).
* deepseek_v4 compressors (HCA / Indexer / CSA): drop the trailing
  `.to(chunk_gate.dtype)`

indexing (layer_types[:-0]). This would trigger an error when the update
method is called, because it will be out of range.

cli-runtime/printers: address review comments on alignment fix

- Promote flushInterval to a package-level const so the regression test
  can reference it instead of hardcoding 100.
- Extend the pre-scan / width-priming path to cover NoHeaders mode.
  Previously, headers were padded to the ultimate max cell width to
  prime tabwriter's RememberWidths across flushes, but with NoHeaders
  there is no header to prime with, so the first flush still fixed
  narrower widths than later rows. Now the first data row is padded
  with the same pre-scanned widths to prime widths identically.
- Hoist lastVisibleCol computation so both the header path and the
  NoHeaders first-row path share it.
- Add a NoHeaders subtest to TestPrintTable_ConsistentAlignmentAcrossFlushes
  and parameterize rowCount on flushInterval.

commit_message:
cli-runtime/printers: optimize table printing for large result sets

Reduce allocations and CPU time in printTable by:

1. Buffering each row into a reusable []byte slice and writing once,
   eliminating ~3 fmt.Fprint calls per cell (tab, value, truncation).

2. Adding a fast path in WriteEscaped that skips the strings.Replacer
   when the string contains no characters needing escaping (>99% of
   cells).

3. Flushing the tabwriter every 100 rows. With RememberWidths enabled,
   the tabwriter retains column widths across flushes, producing
   consistently aligned output while bounding memory from O(rows) to
   O(1).

Benchmark results (AMD Ryzen 9 7950X3D, go1.24):

  name                            old time/op    new time/op    delta
  TablePrinter_10kRows-32          7.71ms         2.57ms        -66.7%
  TablePrinter_100kRows-32         77.4ms         25.6ms        -66.9%
  TablePrinter_500kRows-32          389ms          129ms        -66.9%

  name                            old all

commit_message:
kubelet: fix nil pointer panic in doPodResizeAction when cgroupsPerQOS=false

When cgroupsPerQOS is disabled, the kubelet uses podContainerManagerNoop whose
GetPodCgroupConfig returns (nil, nil). doPodResizeAction then dereferences the
nil ResourceConfig fields (Memory, CPUQuota, CPUShares) causing a panic during
in-place pod vertical scaling.

Handle nil returns from GetPodCgroupConfig by defaulting to an empty
ResourceConfig, and guard all field dereferences with nil checks to safely
treat missing cgroup values as zero.

Fixes #137993

Signed-off-by: Rajneesh Chaudhary <rajneeshrehsaan48@gmail.com>

policy: accept host-only git URLs in extraKnownMarketplaces

ADR-002 describes the `git` source `url` as a free-form `(string)`
the example happens to be a full clone URL, but the schema doesn't
require a repo path. Our marketplace-URI parser was rejecting host-only
HTTPS endpoints (e.g. `https://plugins.internal.example.com`), so
enterprise policy entries with marketplace-registry-style URLs were
silently dropped before they ever reached the UI.

Relax `parseUriMarketplaceReference` to accept host-only URLs and
treat them as a marketplace endpoint identified by host alone. The
canonical id becomes `git:<host>/` so distinct hosts still dedupe
correctly. Existing path-aware behavior is preserved unchanged.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

call site.

markPromiseAsHandled vs setPromiseHandled choice; the rationale lives
in the PR description.

fix(adapters): preserve constraint name in UniqueConstraintViolation error mapping for Postgres-based adapters

When a unique constraint violation (23505) occurs on PostgreSQL, the
constraint name (error.constraint) was previously dropped by adapter-pg,
adapter-neon, and adapter-ppg. Only fields extracted from the detail
message were preserved, which is ambiguous for partial unique indexes
where multiple constraints share the same key columns.

This change preserves the constraint name as { index: error.constraint }
when available, falling back to fields-based extraction otherwise. The
pattern already existed for ForeignKeyConstraintViolation (23503) in all
three adapters, and adapter-mariadb already uses { index } for 1062.

Closes #29495

fix(bootstrap): add scripted mode, reorder deps, capture subprocess errors

Three changes to make `prisma bootstrap` work reliably in non-interactive
environments (AI agents, CI) and improve diagnostics:

1. Scripted mode: when both `--api-key` and `--database` are provided,
   all `confirm()` prompts are auto-accepted. In an empty directory,
   defaults to the `nextjs` template. This removes the TTY requirement
   that caused hangs in Claude Code / Cursor agents.

2. Deps-before-link: the dependency gate (dotenv, prisma, @prisma/client)
   now runs before the link step. Previously, if link failed after init
   but before deps were installed, re-running `prisma bootstrap` crashed
   with "Cannot find module 'dotenv/config'" at config load time.

3. Subprocess stderr capture: `runLocalPrismaCommand` now uses `spawn`
   with a piped stderr stream instead of `execFileSync` with inherited
   stdio. This captures stderr for telemetry while still displaying it
   to the user, and propagates

column whose unique index was dropped in the DB raises Postgres `42P10`

fix(client-engine-runtime): surface unmapped driver errors as user-facing P2039

When a driver adapter error arrived with `kind: 'postgres'` (or `mysql` /
`sqlite` / `mssql`) and the adapter did not map the underlying database
error code to a more specific `MappedError` kind, `rethrowAsUserFacing`
rethrew the raw `DriverAdapterError` unchanged.

Locally, that surfaced as `PrismaClientUnknownRequestError`. Worse, the
query plan executor returned HTTP 500 with the real error message in the
body, and Accelerate strips 500 response bodies, so end users only saw a
generic P6000 with no way to diagnose the underlying problem.

This commonly happens on schema drift — e.g. an `upsert()` targeting a
column whose unique index was dropped in the DB raises Postgres 42P10
("there is no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT
specification"), which is not individually mapped by the adapter. These
errors are not bugs and end users need to see the underlying DB code and

commit_message:
fix(docker): make MongoDB replica set init idempotent

The replica-set init script in the shared MongoDB Dockerfile uses
`until ($MONGO_COMMAND ... rs.initiate(...)); do sleep 1; done` to
wait for mongod to become ready before seeding the replica set. On
first boot this works correctly.

However, when the container is restarted (`docker restart`, `docker
compose up -d` after a stop, host reboot, etc.) with its writable
layer still intact, the replica set config already exists in the data
directory. `rs.initiate()` then returns an `AlreadyInitialized`
error (code 23) with a non-zero exit status, which the `until` loop
treats as "not ready yet" and retries every second, forever. Each
iteration spawns a fresh mongosh process (heavy JS startup) and opens
several connections to mongod, pinning one CPU core and accumulating
hundreds of thousands of leaked connections over time.

Wrap the `rs.initiate(...)` call in a JS try/catch that swallows
only the `AlreadyInitialized` case (by `codeName`

commit_message:
fix(client-engine-runtime): surface unmapped driver errors as user-facing P2039

When a driver adapter error arrived with `kind: 'postgres'` (or `mysql` /
`sqlite` / `mssql`) and the adapter did not map the underlying database
error code to a more specific `MappedError` kind, `rethrowAsUserFacing`
rethrew the raw `DriverAdapterError` unchanged.

Locally, that surfaced as `PrismaClientUnknownRequestError`. Worse, the
query plan executor returned HTTP 500 with the real error message in the
body, and Accelerate strips 500 response bodies, so end users only saw a
generic P6000 with no way to diagnose the underlying problem.

This commonly happens on schema drift — e.g. an `upsert()` targeting a
column whose unique index was dropped in the DB raises Postgres 42P10
("there is no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT
specification"), which is not individually mapped by the adapter. These
errors are not bugs and end users need to see the underlying DB code and
message to debu

fix(client-engine-runtime): surface unmapped driver errors as user-facing P2039

When a driver adapter error arrived with `kind: 'postgres'` (or `mysql` /
`sqlite` / `mssql`) and the adapter did not map the underlying database
error code to a more specific `MappedError` kind, `rethrowAsUserFacing`
rethrew the raw `DriverAdapterError` unchanged.

Locally, that surfaced as `PrismaClientUnknownRequestError`. Worse, the
query plan executor returned HTTP 500 with the real error message in the
body, and Accelerate strips 500 response bodies, so end users only saw a
generic P6000 with no way to diagnose the underlying problem.

This commonly happens on schema drift — e.g. an `upsert()` targeting a
column whose unique index was dropped in the DB raises Postgres 42P10
("there is no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT
specification"), which is not individually mapped by the adapter. These
errors are not bugs and end users need to see the underlying DB code and
message to debu

[Inductor] Fix undefined identifier error in CppWrapper due to false … (#178147)

Description:

When  cpp_wrapper=True  is enabled, the generated C++ code sometimes fails to compile with  error: use of undeclared identifier 'int_array_XXX' . This happens because an
array variable is used in the C++ wrapper code, but its definition ( static constexpr int64_t int_array_XXX[] = ... ) is missing at that specific location.

Root Cause:
In  torch/_inductor/codegen/cpp_wrapper_cpu.py , the  codegen_int_array_var  function uses  id(writeline)  as part of its cache key to avoid generating redundant array
definitions.
However,  writeline  is usually passed as a bound method (e.g.,  self.wrapper_call.writeline ). In Python, accessing a bound method dynamically creates a temporary object.
Once the function call returns, this temporary object is immediately destroyed. Due to Python's memory allocation mechanics, the next time another bound method like
another_buffer.writeline  is dynamically create

Show crate root path in misplaced crate-level attribute diagnostic

coverage: Build the expansion tree around `SyntaxContext`

The expansion tree was previously built around `ExpnId`, which was subtly
incorrect in cases where multiple distinct syntax contexts share the same
`outer_expn` ID. This can occur in the presence of nested macro expansions.

This change turns out to be fairly straightforward, because in all cases we
were obtaining `ExpnId` from `span.ctxt().outer_expn()` anyway, so we can just
remove the call to `.outer_expn()` and use the context instead.

As a result of this change, `context-mismatch-issue-147339.rs` no longer
triggers a context mismatch in `extract_refined_covspans`.

fix: reject pending async deriveds on discard

The rejects all async deriveds of a batch as `OBSOLETE`, so they don't hang around and bail early without triggering the batch.

If we don't do this, an async derived can trigger the already done batch, which schedules an effect that is never flushed. Because it is never flushed the branches it touched on its way up are never cleared, and so anything else in that subtree is now unreactive.

commit_message:
fix: prevent batch unlinking twice

Merged #18298 a bit too soon - there's still a situation which can corrput the linked list: If we merge one batch into another, it will unlink the batch immediately. But `discard` also calls it, running the unlink logic again, which can corrupt the linked list.

Sketch:

1. Batch A is pending.
2. Batch B starts later, intersects A, resolves first, and merges into A.
3. B is unlinked immediately, but `A.oncommit(() => B.discard())` remains.
4. Independent batch C is created while A is still pending and is linked after A.
5. A commits, calls `B.discard()`, and B's stale `#prev`/`#next` can set `A.#next = null` / `last_batch = A`, disconnecting C.

Not able to produce a failing test from it but it's definitely a fix we need to make.

commit_message:
Add F6E3M2FN and F6E2M3FN to xla::PrimitiveType.

This CL introduces first-class declarations for two 6-bit floating point formats:
- F6E3M2FN (3 exponent bits, 2 mantissa bits)
- F6E2M3FN (2 exponent bits, 3 mantissa bits)

These types conform to the OCP Microscaling Formats (MX) specification:
https://www.opencompute.org/documents/ocp-microscaling-formats-mx-v1-0-spec-final-pdf

The encoding parameters are as follows:

FP6 E3M2 (Exponent bias: 3)
- Max normal: +/-28.0
- Min normal: +/-0.25
- Max subnormal: +/-0.1875
- Min subnormal: +/-0.0625

FP6 E2M3 (Exponent bias: 1)
- Max normal: +/-7.5
- Min normal: +/-1.0
- Max subnormal: +/-0.875
- Min subnormal: +/-0.125

PiperOrigin-RevId: 916256455

Add F6E3M2FN and F6E2M3FN to xla::PrimitiveType.

This CL introduces first-class declarations for two 6-bit floating point formats:
- F6E3M2FN (3 exponent bits, 2 mantissa bits)
- F6E2M3FN (2 exponent bits, 3 mantissa bits)

These types conform to the OCP Microscaling Formats (MX) specification:
https://www.opencompute.org/documents/ocp-microscaling-formats-mx-v1-0-spec-final-pdf

The encoding parameters are as follows:

FP6 E3M2 (Exponent bias: 3)
- Max normal: +/-28.0
- Min normal: +/-0.25
- Max subnormal: +/-0.1875
- Min subnormal: +/-0.0625

FP6 E2M3 (Exponent bias: 1)
- Max normal: +/-7.5
- Min normal: +/-1.0
- Max subnormal: +/-0.875
- Min subnormal: +/-0.125

[IFRT] Add simple conversion utilities for `ArrayRef`s and `ValueRef`s

`ToArrays` and `ToValues` converts between a vector of `ArrayRef`s and `ValueRef`s. This makes it simpler to use a few IFRT APIs that take a span of `ValueRef`s instead of `ArrayRef`s.

The only well-supported `Value` type is `Array` for the time being. These conversion utilities will only expect `ArrayRef`s to appear in a span of `ValueRef`s.

commit_message:
Update `shortcircuit_if_known` to `eval_shortcircuit()` (#94163)

Originally this PR was a comment fix that was flagged by @bgw's Claude:

```

  ▎ "Otherwise returns None."

  The function actually returns item_value(last_item) when no element matches.
  Comment doesn't describe behavior.

  ---
  The two most consequential bugs are #1 (swapped AND/OR predicates) and #2 
  (regex). #1 silently produces wrong nullishness/string-ness results for any
  code path that asks about &&/|| chains and feeds into linker decisions; #2
  silently corrupts every default-filter require.context resolution.
``` 

Related to #94159, updates the comment to say that it returns the last
item.

Which appears to be what is happening:

```rust
if it.peek().is_none() {
    return item_value(item);
} 
```

Afterwards, it now includes a reworking of `shortcircuit_if_known` into
`eval_shortcircuit()`:
https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/94163#discussion_r3313537931

`comments: Either<ImmutableComments, Arc<ImmutableComments>>`. The
Either is sized to the wider arm (`ImmutableComments`, ~64 B incl. tag)
and that's an upvar held across every Suspend variant of the closure.
